title: coreJ CDISC rule package
description: Machine-readable schema for the rule packages under rules-legacy/ and rules/ (R-P5, plans/done/PLAN-native-engine-residuals.md). Deliberately permissive where the engine is lenient (the loader disables FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES, so extra fields are allowed everywhere); strict on the shapes the engine actually dispatches on: the package envelope, the Check tree (all/any/not/expression - the operator-leaf alternative was removed with the v1 model, phase 7d), Bindings, Match_Datasets, the Outcome, and the Sensitivity / Executability / Variable_Universe enums (Phase 2 of plans/PLAN-extend-expression-engine.md: the loader fails loud — Rule.loadError, executed as ERROR — on a present-but-unrecognized value for these fields; an absent or null field stays legal). Rule_Type is no longer a rule field (plans/PLAN-leaf-scope-domain-inference.md phase 7): a rule carrying it fails to load.

requirements.description: What the rule needs in order to be able to answer AT ALL (plans/PLAN-scope-requirements-split.md section 4). An unmet requirement is a SKIPPED status naming it, never a finding. All facets are ANDed with each other and with Scope. Typed strictly - unlike the rule level, this block has no legacy shapes to tolerate, and the loader itself rejects an unknown key under it (gate R2).

Variables.description: Column-presence requirements; the successor of the retired Scope.Variables (Include -> All, Exclude -> None). Entry vocabulary: literal, `--` domain-prefix placeholder, qualified DATASET.VARIABLE (Fix #124), glob and /regex/ - each optionally followed by a TYPE TAG ':N' / ':C' (or ':Num' / ':Char', case-insensitive) demanding that the column is numeric or character as well as present. The type is the DATASET's own declared type, never the CDISC Library's or the Define-XML's (ruling D6); a type that cannot be classified does not block (D2). An entry with no tag means exactly what it always did. A requirement is for a thing whose absence means NOTHING TO CHECK - a presence rule must never list the variable it reports.

All.description: Every entry must be present, and of the demanded type when it carries a ':N' / ':C' tag. Byte-for-byte the former Scope.Variables.Include for an untagged entry.

Any.description: AND of ORs. Flat form is ONE group: at least one entry must be present; unmet only when EVERY entry is absent. Nested form is a list of such groups, EVERY group must be met. Two entries minimum per group (loader gate R4): a one-entry group is All with extra ceremony. Mixing strings and groups in one array is a load error (D2). An entry may carry a ':N' / ':C' type tag like an All entry; a group whose entries differ ONLY by tag is R4's one-entry-group error, since the disjunction is just "the variable is present".

None.description: No entry may be present. Byte-for-byte the former Scope.Variables.Exclude. A type suffix is a LOAD ERROR here (gate R9, ruling D1): 'None: [X:N]' would mean "no NUMERIC X may be present", which a character X also satisfies - the opposite of how it reads. Express a type demand in All or Any instead.

All_Or_None.description: Groups spelled exactly like Any (flat = ONE group, nested = several; two distinct entries minimum per group, mixed shape is a load error). A group is satisfied when EVERY entry is present OR NONE is; a partly present group SKIPS the rule with a reason naming the present and the absent halves. Built for a join key that is optional on BOTH sides - [["VISITDY", "TV.VISITDY"]] runs on a study carrying the column on both sides or on neither, and stands down when one side alone has it (the shape on which the join matches nothing and every row is reported). Wildcard entries (glob, /regex/, marker template) are compared RESOLVED: an all-present group additionally needs the entries to match the same concrete column names ([["TRTxxP", "ADSL.TRTxxP"]] runs when no TRTxxP exists anywhere or the same ones exist on both sides). ANDed with All/Any/None and evaluated after them. An entry may also sit in All (a join's first key does, ruling Q9 of the authoring gate); an entry shared with None is a load error (the group could only ever be all-absent), so is a group pairing two pattern shapes (globs compare case-blind, marker templates and /regex/ exactly; differently shaped patterns are not guaranteed to resolve to the same names), and so is a type suffix (the facet decides presence, and a wrongly typed column is neither present nor absent). A filter or _matched_ over a group column is an authoring error: the rule runs when both sides are absent and the bind then fails loud.

Datasets.description: Every listed dataset must be present in the run. Presence is the WIDENED fact ds_exists has tested since Fix #358 - a split domain counts as present - except where the rule reaches the dataset only through a surface that resolves exact (AbsentDatasetSkip.resolvesExactOnly). Entries accept the `--` wildcard, resolved against the primary.

Library.description: Whether a CDISC Library metadata provider is required. DERIVED: the assembler materialises it and the engine behaves on the derivation regardless; an authored value that disagrees is a load error (gate R5).

Define.description: Whether a sponsor Define-XML overlay is required. Derived - see Library.

Dictionary.description: Whether at least one external dictionary is required. A boolean, not a list of external_dictionary_type values - the types are already in the Bindings and a second copy would only give them a second chance to drift. Derived - see Library.

datasetScope.description: Scope.Datasets (owner requirement #5) - selection by the dataset NAME. Deliberately not the Domains shape: there is no split-base re-test (Domains: [LB] selects LB1/LB2; Datasets: [LB] selects the file called LB and nothing else) and no include_split_datasets, which is a statement about domain families and means nothing on a name axis. Entry vocabulary is Domains': ALL / NONE sentinels, /regex/, glob, the strict `--` token, literal. Glob, regex and NONE are coreJ-only and not upstream-portable.

Severity.description: Rule severity: the level this rule's finding reports at. Absent means Error, and Error is therefore never written (RuleCanonicalizer strips it). Notice is a report-only kind and is not authorable.

Scope.description: Which datasets the rule is ABOUT - selection, never a verdict (plans/PLAN-scope-requirements-split.md section 4.1). Classes, Domains, Datasets, Data_Structures, Subclasses, Use_Case. Deliberately left untyped apart from Datasets (PLAN-scope-data-structures-subclasses.md): the axes are validated byte-exactly at load, and a schema copy of the closed vocabularies would be a second place to drift. Scope carries NO Variables block: it retired to Requirements.Variables, and a surviving one is a load error on a corpus rule (loader gate R1) because the engine model no longer binds it.

Precondition.$comment: Deliberately the PLAIN check, never checkOrLevels: a Precondition is a property of the rule, not of a level. It is evaluated ONCE, before any level runs.
Precondition.description: ENGINE-INTERNAL, not an authorable field (owner ruling Q3, loader gate R8). It carries machine-emitted dependency-availability gates - library_available() / dictionary_available(<type>) / available(<call>) - which RulePackageLoader injects at load and OperationInliner bakes into the shipped packages offline. It is declared here because this schema validates the assembled rules/ view, where such a term is legitimate; deleting the definition would red every dictionary-gated package. An AUTHORED Precondition in rules-src/checks fails to load - see rule-check.schema.json, which does not declare the field.

Output_Variables.description: The variables a finding reports. A leading `!` marks an EXCLUSION (`!X` removes the auto-derived X from the effective list; `!--X`, `!$id`, `!DS.COL` likewise) — `--X` is always an include. Every entry must be double-quoted in YAML (an unquoted `!X` is a YAML tag). The pattern rejects a bare `!` and a stacked `!!X`; the loader's E-3 validation judges the rest.

Bindings.description: Phase 7b (owner rulings 2026-09-17): the operation bindings, each entry exactly name + expression. The retired Operations:/id:/field-form spellings are load errors; see rule-check.schema.json for the authored-source twin of this definition.

Expansion.description: Fix #147 / EC-56 - declared-token template expansion. Java-only: the Python reference engine ignores the block and reads the template literally. See CORE-RULES-SPECIFICATION.md, Extension Fields - Expansion.

Grouping_Variables.description: The flat, legacy spelling of the rule-level grouping key. Still accepted by the Java loader, and the only spelling the Python-facing rules-legacy/ view carries (LegacyGroupingDegrader flattens the block back to it). Mutually exclusive with Grouping - declaring both is a load error.

Grouping.description: Fix #180 - the rule-level grouping block: the grouping key plus its keep_missings disposition. Java-only: the Python reference engine has no channel for keep_missings, so the legacy view is degraded back to the flat Grouping_Variables and the parameter is dropped. Mutually exclusive with Grouping_Variables.

Variable_Universe.description: PLAN-leaf-scope-domain-inference.md section 3.7 - which variables the VAR cursor iterates for a rule whose evaluation domain carries that cursor: Data (default when absent; the dataset's columns in column order) or Define (the Define-XML ItemDefs of the domain in ItemDef order; no Define-XML provider means SKIPPED). Iteration only - Requirements.Variables still filters within the universe. Never derived from operand classes. Define on a Check with no variable cursor is a load error.

checkOrLevels.description: A rule's Check is EITHER one condition OR a map of check levels (plans/done/PLAN-severity-and-check-levels.md section 3.3). A Check whose keys are ALL ladder level names is a level map; a Check with NO level-name key is a plain condition, exactly as before. A MIXED map ({ERROR: ..., expression: ...}) and an UNKNOWN level name are load errors - the discrimination is total and free because every condition key is lower-case and every level name UPPER-case. A single Check: is one level, at the rule's effective Severity; the strictest declared level of a level map MUST equal the rule's Severity, and disagreeing is a load error. Bindings, Scope, Requirements, Grouping, Match_Datasets, Precondition and Outcome.Output_Variables are shared across all of a rule's levels - a rule that needs different ones is two rules. NOTE the run severity threshold is NOT expressible here or anywhere else in a package: it is a RUN option only (CLI --severity-level / REST CheckRunRequest.severityThreshold / .cdt #runLevel), and a package or rule declaring any spelling of it is a load error.

plainCheck.description: A Check that declares no level at all - one condition, one level, at the rule's effective Severity. The propertyNames clause is what makes a MIXED map ({ERROR: ..., expression: ...}) invalid: without it the mixed map would satisfy this branch (the condition shapes tolerate extra keys, because the loader runs with FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES off) and the oneOf would match exactly once and pass. It uses the ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$ level-SHAPED test the deserialiser (RuleCheckDeserializer.LEVEL_SHAPED) uses, not an enumeration of the four canonical names: enumerating the names accepted a mixed map whose level key was misspelled or non-canonical ({CRITICAL: ..., expression: ...}), which the loader rejects. Every legitimate condition key (all/any/not/expression, the leaf fields) is lower-case, so no well-formed plain Check carries an all-caps key. Known residual: a mixed-CASE mis-spelt level key ({Error: ...}) is not level-shaped and still passes this branch - the loader's parseOrNull dispatch catches it.

levelMap.description: The level-keyed Check: every key is one of REJECT / ERROR / WARNING / INFO, and no other key is allowed. Notice is a report-only kind the engine produces and no rule may author, so it is not a level here. Evaluation runs strictest first (REJECT -> ERROR -> WARNING -> INFO) whatever order the levels were authored in, and first claim wins per finding unit: a row claimed by a stricter level is never re-reported by a weaker one.

levelCheck.description: One level's value: the Check condition that level evaluates, optionally carrying that level's own Message. A level that declares no Message falls back to the rule's Outcome.Message, resolved at report time from the claiming level - the rule message is never copied into the levels.

Message.description: This level's message; absent means the rule's Outcome.Message.

check.$comment: The operator-leaf alternative ({ operator:, name:, value:, value_is_literal:, regex:, prefix:, suffix:, within:, ordering:, ... }) was REMOVED on 2026-09-17 together with its leaf $def. Phase 7d of plans/PLAN-typed-expression-engine.md deleted the v1 operator-leaf model whole (ExprLowering, CheckConditionLeaf, CheckOperator), and CheckConditionDeserializer now REJECTS a Check node carrying operator: with a message naming expression: as the replacement. While the alternative stood, this schema validated a rule the loader refuses - a machine-readable document asserting the opposite of the engine, which is worse than a stale sentence because something downstream believes it. Corpus at removal: 0 files with an operator-leaf Check.

token.description: The exact string substituted wherever it occurs in the rule body. Author-chosen; must carry a non-alphanumeric sigil so it can never collide with a CDISC variable name (R-5.17).

over.description: The binding source. Closed and extensible: a third source costs one new value here plus its resolver in TokenExpander.

with.description: shared_variables only - the foreign dataset whose variables are intersected with the dataset under validation.

pattern.description: domain_from_variable only - the column-name shape the token appears in; the token position is the capture. Must contain the token.

known_domain_only.description: domain_from_variable only - keep only captures the library attests as dataset names. This is what excludes ADaM's own ASEQ / SRCSEQ / RECSEQ.
